Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Nina, 6:35: yes, please hold it there, and don't scan the pallet label as received yet. i'll compare the carton marks with the delivery note
Luis, 6:41: i'm at door 4 now. carton 24 has a second label folded under the top flap, maybe that's why it wasn't on the list, but i'll verify

Omar, 6:51: checking now. it comes up as scanned at 15:08 yesterday, but the location field is blank, so it may be a duplicate scan
Luis, 6:56: that matches my notes. yesterday's batch had a retry after the wifi dropped, and i wasn't sure if the last carton went through
Nina, 7:03: okay, leave the pallet on hold while i ask inventory to review the batch. use the other 23 cartons only if they're clean and count matches
Omar, 7:11: all 23 on the list have readable labels, and the quantities match. i moved those to reserve shelf R-14, not the pick face
Nina, 7:14: perfect, please record R-14 in the receiving sheet. i'll keep carton 24 at the marked hold spot beside the scale
Luis, 7:22: quick note, the printer at desk 2 is feeding labels slightly crooked. the left edge is fine, but the barcode is close to the right margin
Nina, 7:26: thanks for flagging. use printer 1 for relabels until maintenance checks it, and leave the test strip taped to desk 2 for them
Omar, 7:34: printer 1 is busy with the returns batch. i can queue the replacement labels after that, unless Luis needs one right away for the open case
Luis, 7:38: not urgent. carton 24 is still closed, and the original label can be read from the side, so i'll wait for inventory's note
Nina, 7:46: 1) scan each carton label once 2) confirm the quantity on screen before moving it 3) if a barcode errors, park the carton at hold and message here
Omar, 7:51: added. one thing, the scanner on cart 5 beeped twice on carton 6, but it only added one unit. i checked the screen before moving it
Nina, 7:55: thanks, that's okay. if it beeps twice again, stop and send me the carton number; don't rescan unless the screen shows zero
Luis, 8:04: inventory replied: yesterday's batch shows one completed scan for carton 24, no location update. they haven't confirmed where it was put yet
Nina, 8:09: got it. please keep the hold tag on it, and don't change the received status until inventory confirms whether it physically arrived yesterday
Omar, 8:17: i found the tag printer roll is almost out, about 15 labels left. there's a full roll in cabinet B, top drawer, by the spare batteries
Luis, 8:21: i'll swap it after this returns batch. the cabinet key is back on the hook, and i'll put the empty roll on the desk for supplies
Nina, 8:29: appreciate it. also, the morning carrier is booked for 9:30, so keep the aisle between door 4 and the scale clear for their cages
Omar, 8:36: aisle is clear now. there are two empty cages against the yellow line near returns, not blocking the route, but i can move them if needed
Nina, 8:40: please move those beside the blue rack, not in front of the extinguisher. the driver asked us to keep that corner open last week
Omar, 8:44: moved them to the blue rack. one wheel on the smaller cage sticks a little, so i parked it with the handle facing out
Luis, 8:53: printer 1 is free now, and i ran one test label. the barcode scans clean from about a foot away, so i'm printing the three replacements
Nina, 9:02: okay, label only the three cartons from lot 81B, not carton 24. send me a photo of the labels before you apply them
Luis, 9:10: photo sent in the thread. all three labels show lot 81B and the carton numbers match the packing list; i haven't applied them yet
Nina, 9:14: looks good. go ahead and apply those, then scan each carton once and tell me if the screen accepts all three without an error
Omar, 9:22: all three scanned and moved to R-14. the screen accepted them, and i updated the receiving sheet with the shelf and count
Luis, 9:31: inventory says carton 24 wasn't assigned a location in the batch, and they're still checking the physical count from yesterday. hold spot stays the same for now
Nina, 9:38: understood. we'll leave it on hold through shift change, and i'll add a note for the afternoon lead to check with inventory before releasing it", "output": "MODE: /slack

We’re seeing intermittent misses on the west-side barcode scanners again. The cartons still move through the conveyor, but the scan event doesn’t show up in the receiving dashboard until someone scans the label a second time. Has anyone seen this on another lane?

Leon — 8:15 AM: I noticed it on lane 4 around 7:40. The first scan beeped, and the scanner screen showed the carton ID, but the dashboard stayed blank. I wrote down three examples before the next pallet arrived: BX-48192, BX-48197, and BX-48203.

Maya — 8:18 AM: Thanks, Leon. Are those all cartons from the same supplier or the same label batch? I’m trying to separate a label-quality issue from a reader or network problem. The labels looked fine from my station, but I haven’t checked them up close.

Leon — 8:22 AM: Same supplier, Northstar Packaging, but two different purchase orders. The barcode is Code 128, printed in black on a white label. I checked the quiet zones on BX-48197, and they look clear; no tape or folded corners over the bars.

Priya — 8:26 AM: We had a similar delay on lane 2 last Thursday, but that was after the access point rebooted. Is the west scanner connected to AP-WH-07? I can check the connection logs if someone confirms the scanner’s asset tag.

Maya — 8:29 AM: It’s scanner WS-14, asset tag 006731. The status page says it’s connected to AP-WH-07, and I’m not seeing a disconnect alert. The problem is hard to reproduce; it happened twice in about ten minutes, then stopped.

Derek — 8:34 AM: I’m near lane 4 now. The trigger is responding, and the scan window looks clean. I scanned a test label five times; all five appeared in the dashboard within a second. I’ll watch the next inbound pallet rather than change settings yet.

Maya — 8:39 AM: Good call. One detail from the receiving crew: they said, “It beeps like normal, but the carton isn’t in my list.” They weren’t sure whether the screen beep came from the scanner or the handheld terminal, though.

Priya — 8:43 AM: The handheld uses a different reader, so that distinction matters. Could someone note whether the scanner display shows the full carton ID at the moment of the beep? Also, please include the time to the nearest minute if it happens again.

Derek — 8:48 AM: Just caught one. At 8:46, BX-48219 beeped on WS-14 and the scanner display showed the full ID. No row appeared in the dashboard for roughly 35 seconds. Then the row appeared without another scan, so it may be a delayed event rather than a missed read.

Maya — 8:52 AM: That’s useful. Did the carton stay at the induction point for those 35 seconds, or had it already passed the diverter? I want to know whether the delay affects the physical routing or only what the receiving crew sees on screen.

Derek — 8:57 AM: It had passed the diverter and was waiting at the end of the belt. The lane light stayed green, and the carton went to the expected staging area. The crew held it there because the dashboard entry wasn’t visible yet.

Leon — 9:03 AM: I checked the other two IDs from my notes. BX-48192 appeared about 20 seconds after its scan, while BX-48197 appeared immediately on the second scan. BX-48203 is still in the dashboard history, but its event time is 7:51.

Priya — 9:08 AM: I’m seeing several brief spikes in AP-WH-07 latency between 7:35 and 8:05, but no full disconnect. The log records retries at 7:42 and 7:51. I can’t tell from this view whether those retries delayed scanner events or just routine status traffic.

Maya — 9:13 AM: Could you share the latency range and whether it overlaps those carton times? I’m not asking anyone to change the access point configuration yet. If the timing lines up, we can give support a focused set of examples instead of guessing.

Priya — 9:18 AM: The spikes reached 480–620 ms, with most readings under 90 ms. The 7:42 retry lines up with Leon’s first example; the 7:51 retry may line up with BX-48203. I don’t have a precise scan timestamp for that carton.

Derek — 9:24 AM: I found a photo of the lane 4 setup from yesterday’s cleanup. WS-14 is mounted above the belt, about 1.8 meters from the carton path, and the bracket doesn’t look loose. There’s a new metal guard beside the cable tray, installed Monday.

Leon — 9:29 AM: The guard is about 30 centimeters from the scanner cable, not the scanner head. It was added to keep empty totes from hitting the tray. I haven’t noticed the signal indicator flicker, but I can check the cable route during the next lull.

Maya — 9:35 AM: Please do, and don’t move the bracket while the lane is running. Also, can we get one clean comparison from lane 3 using the same Northstar label batch? That might tell us whether the delay follows the labels or stays with WS-14.

Derek — 9:42 AM: Lane 3 has the same supplier batch coming in after lunch. I can scan a few cartons there and record the dashboard times, then compare them with lane 4. I’ll use the carton IDs and minute-level timestamps, not photos of the labels.

Priya — 9:48 AM: I can pull the scanner event log for WS-14 if we have a 15-minute window. It includes received time and device time, but the display doesn’t show the carton ID in every row. Does 7:35–7:55 cover the examples well enough?

Maya — 9:53 AM: Yes, that window should cover the first reports. Please include the AP latency entries in the same export if that’s easy. We’re not sure yet that they’re related, and I’d rather keep the log review to those times.

Leon — 10:01 AM: I checked the cable route. It’s secured, the connector is fully seated, and there’s no visible damage. The status indicator stayed solid while I gently moved the cable at the strain relief. I didn’t unplug anything or change the scanner settings.

Derek — 10:07 AM: I’ve put a note on the lane board asking the crew to record the scan time and carton ID if the dashboard entry is delayed. I also told them to keep the carton in the expected staging area and call the floor lead if the route looks wrong.

Maya — 10:12 AM: Thanks, everyone. Could someone from support help us compare WS-14’s event timestamps with AP-WH-07’s latency around 7:42 and 7:51? We have a few delayed entries, but no confirmed routing error, and we haven’t changed any settings.

Priya — 10:17 AM: I’ll attach the limited log window and the three carton IDs to the support thread. I’ll label the times as approximate where we don’t have an exact scan timestamp. I’ve got the revised scene order for Friday’s radio drama session in the shared folder. I moved the market scene ahead of the station announcement so the sound team can set up the crowd bed first.

Dev: Thanks, I’ll check the page numbers against my script copy before lunch. I’m bringing the portable recorder, two spare cables, and the paper release forms. The recorder’s battery was low after Tuesday’s read-through, so I’ll charge it at my desk.

Nina: I can print the updated cast list and mark the characters who need to be in the first booth block. Should I include the understudy notes on that copy, or keep those in the production folder?

Mara: Keep them in the folder for now; the cast list can stay uncluttered. I’ll also send the actors the new arrival time once the studio confirms the room.

Dev: I’ll label the ambience files by location instead of scene number, since a few cues repeat. If anyone has a preference, let me know before I export them.
